To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed and tested a novel registration method for the liver, which allows the user to specify anisotropic landmark uncertainties.
we developed a novel registration method that allows for a combined intensity-landmark based registration and can handle anisotropy of the localization uncertainties of the landmarks.
we propose a general framework for the incorporation of landmark information in a non rigid image registration approach that allows anisotropic localization tolerances.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new registration approach for non rigid image registration with a special consideration of anisotropic landmark uncertainties.
the development of an anisotropic landmark constrained registration method for the registration of medical images.
the development of a robust and accurate non rigid registration method with the help of user knowledge in the form of landmarks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the incorporation of user knowledge in form of landmark constraints can improve the registration results significantly.
the presented method is able to incorporate anisotropic tolerances for landmark constraints into an intensity based non rigid registration framework.
the presented registration approach is an effective way to integrate additional user knowledge into a registration process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have presented a general framework for a combined intensity and feature based registration scheme.
the presented approach is able to handle the complex deformations of soft tissues and to restrict the number and the type of possible deformations by using a small set of corresponding landmarks.
the presented registration scheme can handle anisotropically localized landmarks and can be applied to a wide range of image modalities and anatomies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the usage of corresponding vessels in the registration process can be a promising approach for the registration of images containing soft tissue.
anisotropic localization uncertainty can be modeled in the registration framework and that it is possible to incorporate such knowledge into the registration scheme in a consistent way.
the usage of corresponding segments of vessels is an important tool to increase the robustness of the registration process.
